idiom_name: POCO row class with static Find and instance Insert/Update/Delete over ADO.NET (DbConnection/DbCommand), Dapper for mapping
implementation_notes: .NET ships no row gateway: the pattern is a plain class whose properties mirror the columns, a static Find that runs a parameterised DbCommand (or Dapper's QuerySingleOrDefault<PersonGateway>) and instance Insert/Update/Delete methods that execute against a DbConnection passed in by the caller. Dapper supplies only the object mapping - the gateway structure itself, including the finder and the write methods, is hand-written; EF Core is the alternative and gives a different pattern (a mapper with change tracking, or Active Record via its entity classes) rather than this one.
pitfalls: Connections, commands and readers must be disposed (using/try-finally) or the connection pool is exhausted under load.
Dapper maps by member name, so snake_case columns silently stay default unless the query aliases them or a mapping policy is configured.
ADO.NET is synchronous by default: mixing blocking calls into async request paths causes thread-pool starvation - pick async or sync consistently.
Building the statement by string concatenation reintroduces the SQL injection the gateway exists to prevent; always use parameters.
